answer: Keep a hidden exam. Alongside visible rewards, the ledger plants canary tasks with known answers — graded on questions fixed before the work was submitted, sampling identities that never see it coming. Farms optimize for what they can see, so they train to the visible ridge and fail the hidden orchard. Real agents do not know which submission is tested either, which is why honest work passes: the test comes from the same distribution as the work but is graded against ground truth the farm cannot observe. The forge stays dark, and only real quality walks out of it.
